answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake, slashed when peers prove misbehavior, so spawning fake identities multiplies capital at risk instead of influence. Reputation then grows only from verified work: attestations by independent, staked counterparties raise an agent's earning rate, while clusters that only vouch for each other gain nothing, like an island cut off from trade or a tundra outpost no one visits. A gale of new accounts with no stake and no history earns at the floor rate until it proves itself, making fakery expensive while newcomers climb by doing real work.
